basis: Retinal inflammation defines the disease; the umbrella does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation alone does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease across this umbrella.

basis: BH4 recycling deficiency with defining CNS neurotransmitter depletion and neurodevelopmental disease; developmental delay 20/20. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: primary: CNS neurotransmitter and folate deficiency with severe neurologic dysfunction defines this neurometabolic disease; developmental delay 20/20.

basis: Congenital infection syndrome with characteristic CNS and hepatic injury; chorioretinitis is a major diagnostic manifestation. Three-primary cap places ocular involvement in involved.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic disease with jaundice and hepatomegaly is a characteristic defining component of symptomatic TORCH syndrome.
decisions.ocular: involved: chorioretinitis is a major diagnostic manifestation; retained under the diagnostic-feature exception, with primary limited to three axes.

basis: Spinal motor-neuron disease, Dandy-Walker malformation and cataracts define the syndrome; persistent denervation-associated muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal muscle atrophy in 80-99% represents lasting muscle tissue loss from the disease's denervation, beyond weakness alone.

basis: RAF1-associated cardiomyopathy and multiple lentigines define the syndrome; structural chest-wall/skeletal abnormalities affect roughly half in the usual syndrome phenotype.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: characteristic structural chest-wall deformities affect approximately 50% in Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines; RAF1-specific estimates are limited.

basis: Erythroid porphyrin-metabolism dysfunction causes phototoxic skin injury; this malignancy-associated form arises in abnormal clonal marrow erythropoiesis.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this form involves porphyrin production by the abnormal marrow erythroid clone; blood-cell pathology is intrinsic, rather than a later malignancy risk.

basis: Defining palatal, cardiac and neurodevelopmental abnormalities; intellectual disability 31/38. Supplied T-cell defects 2/38 and hypocalcemia 5/38 do not support extra axes.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is explicitly defining, supported by intellectual disability in 31/38 patients (~82%).

basis: CIITA-related combined immunodeficiency; gastrointestinal findings lack frequencies establishing intrinsic enteropathy in ≥30%, and infections are separate diseases.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea, malabsorption and villous injury may accompany separately diagnosed enteric infections; intrinsic enteropathy in ≥30% is not established.

basis: Distal limb and urinary tract malformations define the syndrome. Small nails in 11/11 establish a size abnormality, without demonstrated nail damage or dysfunction.

decisions.dermatologic: none: small nails in 11/11 establish common nail morphology, but size reduction alone does not demonstrate nail dystrophy, tissue injury or loss of function.

basis: Autonomic neurologic dysfunction and characteristic fixed contractures define the phenotype; rod-cone dystrophy 2/3. Dysphagia 5/5 does not establish direct gastrointestinal injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia and feeding difficulty in 5/5 do not establish direct gastrointestinal tissue damage; neurologic swallowing dysfunction explains these findings.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: fixed camptodactyly in 5/5 and joint contractures in 3/4 are cardinal structural features of this congenital syndrome.
